provisional_claims.summary: History exchange: _common_bases truncated maximal common ancestors to one (maximal[:1]), so criss-cross reconciliation (both collaborators previously combined the same work) used an incomplete merge base and could lose later edits/reversions; now all maximal bases are recursively combined.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Two installations reconcile the same concurrent pair independently (M1, M2), continue work on each, then reconcile again; common bases {L1,R1} truncated to one, treating the other's changes as concurrent edits.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange: reconciliation was order-dependent — reconcile(L,R) placed R's concurrent actions before L's, so two collaborators who each combined the same pair (own publication first) produced contradictory action orders and the next round of reconciliation failed with an order-conflict (losing later edits/reversions). Reconcile now merges the pair in canonical (sorted publication id) order, matching the sorted parents and sorted virtual-base construction, so independent combinations of the same work are identical.

Each edits its merged checkout, publishes, exchanges, reconcile again -> HistoryConflict order-conflict. After fix both merges are identical (same revision) and round 2/3 merge cleanly retaining 'desk edited', 'field edited' and a later reversion.
